incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Act of Taiwan (公司法), Chapter IV (Limited Company), Articles 98-113 and Article 387 (registration); Company Registration Rules (公司之登記及認許辦法); Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals (外國人投資條例) Articles 5-7; for mainland-China shareholders, Regulations Governing Investment in Taiwan by Mainland Area Investors (大陸地區人民來台投資許可辦法).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commerce (商業發展署), Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan, operating the Company Registration One-Stop Online Portal (公司登記一站式線上申請平台); incorporation filing for Taipei-based companies may be electronically routed to the Department of Economic Development, Taipei City Government (台北市政府產業發展局).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation Registration (公司設立登記申請書) together with the Articles of Incorporation (公司章程), unanimous Shareholders' Written Consent (股東同意書), and Director's Consent to Serve (董事願任同意書).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum registered capital after the 2009 liberalization; however, the entire subscribed capital must be fully paid up into a New Taiwan Dollar escrow bank account and certified by a licensed Taiwan CPA (Capital Verification Report) before the incorporation certificate is issued. Inward foreign-exchange remittance must match the approved investment amount, and repatriation or withdrawal of capital within the first three years requires MOEA approval; mainland investors must additionally respect the escrow and timing conditions indorsed on the mainland investment approval letter.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: As the unanimous shareholder's written consent acting as the First Board Resolution, it is RESOLVED: (1) The Articles of Incorporation, as presented, are adopted for filing with the Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs. (2) The subscribed registered capital must be fully deposited by the sole shareholder into the designated escrow bank account before incorporation and released upon issuance of the registration certificate. (3) The registered-office address stated in the Articles is adopted as the statutory domicile for service of process. (4) [Name] is appointed first Director and General Manager with power to open bank accounts and execute tax, labor, and insurance registrations. This consent is effective immediately and supersedes all prior notices.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Investment Review (投資審議司), Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan (successor to the Investment Commission), online at the MOEA investment application portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the standardized investor application electronically before any inward capital remittance. The sole shareholder must declare the ultimate beneficial owner, remittance route, and capital source; select the approved business scope matching ISIC 7110 (engineering services and related technical consulting) and certify non-involvement in restricted fields under the negative list for mainland investment. Await the approving instrument before opening the capital escrow account.
required_dossiers: Foreign/Mainland Investor Investment Application Form (投資申請書)
Certificate of incorporation or identity certification of the sole shareholder
Beneficial ownership and source-of-funds declaration
Notarized power of attorney appointing the local Taiwan agent
Business plan describing offshore BIM/CAD drafting services, target clients, and staffing
Audited financial statements of the mainland parent/shareholder for the last fiscal year
Negative-list compliance affidavit and capital remittance commitment letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or returned, submit supplementary explanations and documentation within the statutory 45-day cure period; if the intended scope is judged restricted, amend the scope wording to unsealed drafting and modeling services that do not constitute certified engineering practice, or apply for discretionary case-by-case review under Article 8 of the mainland investment regulations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Approval (名稱及業務預查)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce (商業發展署), Ministry of Economic Affairs, accessed via the Company Registration One-Stop Online Portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit electronically up to three proposed Chinese names each ending with 有限公司, together with the corresponding English name, and the proposed business scope text drawn from the Taiwan Standard Industrial Classification code 7110 (工程服務及相關技術顧問業). The pre-approval certificate remains valid for four months and must be exhibited at incorporation.
required_dossiers: Electronic name and business scope pre-application form
Three candidate Chinese company names with English equivalents
Reference number of the investment approval letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name conflicts with a priority-registered name, substitute the next candidate name and resubmit; if the proposed business scope wording is broad enough to imply licensed engineering practice, narrow the text to offshore BIM modeling, CAD drafting, and technical document production.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Remittance, Escrow Deposit, and CPA Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Approved Taiwan foreign-exchange bank (acting as escrow custodian) and a CPA licensed under the Certified Public Accountants Act of Taiwan.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After investment approval, remit the approved capital amount from the overseas shareholder to the company's dedicated inward-remittance account. Instruct the bank to convert the funds and hold them in the company's capital escrow account; instruct the CPA to examine the bank certificate and shareholders' consent, and to issue a Capital Verification Report certifying full payment of the subscribed capital.
required_dossiers: Investment approval certificate
Foreign-exchange inward remittance certificate issued by the receiving bank
Executed capital escrow account agreement
Unanimous shareholders' consent authorizing the capital structure
CPA Capital Verification Report (資本額查核報告書)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the remitting bank imposes anti-money-laundering queries, deliver the underlying equity subscription agreement and the investor's corporate KYC pack; if the CPA queries the genuineness of funds, supplement the bank statement trails from the remitting and receiving banks and re-attest the verification report.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Registration Filing (設立登記申請)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs, through the Company Registration One-Stop Online Portal, with delegated processing by the Taipei City Department of Economic Development for the registered office in Taipei.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the completed incorporation application together with the Articles of Incorporation, unanimous shareholders' consent, director's consent, CPA capital verification report, name pre-approval certificate, investment approval letter, lease agreement, and building-use consent. Pay the NT$1,000 minimum registration fee online and submit the application for the administrative review; the authority will issue the electronic incorporation certificate upon approval.
required_dossiers: Incorporation Registration Application Form (公司設立登記申請書)
Articles of Incorporation signed by the sole shareholder (公司章程)
Unanimous Shareholders' Written Consent (股東同意書)
Director's Consent to Serve (董事願任同意書)
CPA Capital Verification Report
Lease agreement and landlord building-use consent (租賃契約及使用同意書)
Building tax receipt or ownership certificate of the registered office
Company name and business scope pre-approval certificate
Investment approval certificate
Proof of registration fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar marks the file for correction (e.g., defective lease documentation or inconsistent scope wording), cure all defects within the notified period and resubmit electronically; if registration is refused, file an administrative appeal with the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days together with the corrected dossier.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Taiwan (Republic of China) — Tax Administration (財政部賦稅署) with five regional National Taxation Bureaus (各地區國稅局) as the operational registration and audit authorities; primary online portal: 財政部稅務入口網 (https://www.etax.nat.gov.tw); e-invoice portal: 財政部電子發票整合服務平台 (https://www.einv.nat.gov.tw); company and tax one-stop registration portal: 財政部商工登記一站式線上申請作業 (https://onestop.nat.gov.tw).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A mainland-China-funded incorporator must first obtain investment permission from the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs (投審會投資許可) under the Regulations on Permission of Investment in Taiwan by People from Mainland China; upon approval, the WFOE (有限公司) is incorporated through the Ministry of Economic Affairs company registration system, which simultaneously generates the 8-digit Unified Business Number (統一編號, the sole TIN used for both income tax and VAT); since April 2019 the tax registration (稅籍登記) is automatically synchronised with company registration through the one-stop online platform, and the new entity receives a tax-registration notification from the local National Taxation Bureau; the entity must then open a Taiwan foreign-exchange deposit account, complete labour-insurance registration, and separately apply for electronic Uniform Invoice issuance credentials (電子發票開立人註冊) with a Turnkey transmission certificate before issuing invoices; a foreign shareholder without a Taiwan address must appoint a tax agent (稅務代理人) or a domiciled fiscal representative to receive tax filings and withholding returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the Taiwan-incorporated, mainland-China-invested WFOE is a resident profit-seeking enterprise (營利事業) taxed on worldwide income at the flat 20% corporate income tax rate, with an additional 5% retained-earnings surtax on undistributed surplus (Income Tax Act Articles 3, 5 and 66-9); dividend distributions to the mainland-China corporate shareholder are subject to a 21% non-resident dividend withholding tax (Articles 88 and 92) unless a cross-strait double-taxation arrangement lowering the rate has been rendered effective and is applied by the withholding agent; the entity is not a pass-through vehicle and has no territorial tax exemption; a foreign parent operating directly in Taiwan without incorporation would instead be taxed as a non-resident branch on Taiwan-source income only.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Taiwan has no check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election regime. Available taxpayer elections most relevant to a WFOE: (1) simplified small-scale VAT election — with National Taxation Bureau approval, average monthly sales between NT$40,001 and NT$200,000 (services) may be taxed at 1% of tax-inclusive sales with no Uniform Invoice obligation; (2) voluntary VAT registration — a business below the NT$40,000/NT$80,000 starting point may still register as a full 5% VAT taxpayer to recover input credits; (3) deemed-income election under Article 25 of the Income Tax Act — a foreign related party with no Taiwan fixed place of business may elect, through its Taiwan withholding agent and with bureau approval, deemed net-profit taxation at 15% of service contract revenue (and 25% for certain technical services) instead of the standard 20% gross withholding on Taiwan-source service fees; (4) dividend-distribution election — the WFOE may time and elect distributions to manage the interaction between the 5% retained-earnings surtax and the 21% non-resident dividend withholding tax; (5) e-invoice transmission-mode election — the taxpayer may choose Turnkey direct transmission, Web-service API, or cloud-invoice service mode for satisfying e-invoice clearance obligations.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT — Business Tax (加值型及非加值型營業稅法, Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax Act)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory VAT registration within 15 days of business commencement — no general de minimis economic-turnover exemption for registered enterprises. Relief thresholds: average monthly sales of services not exceeding NT$40,000 (goods: NT$80,000) are below the tax starting point (起徵點) and may be exempt from registration and tax; sales between the starting point and NT$200,000 per month qualify for the small-scale taxpayer scheme at 1% VAT (no Uniform Invoice issuance); sales exceeding NT$200,000 per month require full VAT registration with Uniform Invoice issuance and the standard 5% rate. A foreign enterprise without a Taiwan fixed place of business supplying cross-border electronic services into Taiwan becomes liable for simplified VAT registration when annual Taiwan-source sales exceed NT$480,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: A mandatory electronic Uniform Invoice (電子發票) regime operates through the Ministry of Finance E-Invoice Integration Service Platform. Every full VAT-registered business must issue e-invoices in the prescribed E-Invoice Standard (Turnkey) data format and transmit invoice data to the platform in real time; B2C cloud invoices must be transmitted within 48 hours of issuance, and B2B invoices for zero-rated export services within 7 calendar days, each invoice carrying a random-number stamp (隨機碼) and QR code for buyer verification; zero-rated export sales must be flagged as such on the e-invoice. The platform cross-checks invoice transmission against customs export declarations and Foreign Exchange Department record data. Failure or late transmission of e-invoice data incurs per-invoice fines of NT$1,500 to NT$30,000 under the Business Tax Act e-invoice penalty provisions, and habitual breaches may trigger suspension of Uniform Invoice issuance and audit-led reassessment at 5% VAT.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 7 of the Business Tax Act, a zero rate (0% VAT with full input-credit refund) applies to (a) exported goods; and (b) services rendered in Taiwan but used outside Taiwan and paid for in foreign currency, including offshore BIM and structural CAD drafting delivered to a non-resident principal. Eligibility for the Taiwan WFOE requires: (1) the counterparty is established outside Taiwan and does not resell or consume the service inside Taiwan; (2) the BIM/CAD deliverables are used and enjoyed abroad — design files, drawings and models supplied to an overseas contractor or foreign project owner satisfy the use-abroad test; (3) the consideration is invoiced in and received in foreign currency (whether via wire transfer, Wise payout, or converted NT$ after inward remittance); (4) the zero-rated nature is stated on the electronic Uniform Invoice and the export-service file is identified in the bi-monthly VAT return (Form 401/403). Goods exports must additionally comply with customs export declaration requirements. The zero-rating claim is asserted at filing time, and the resultant excess input VAT is refundable on the bi-monthly return.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (出口報單) for goods shipments, or a comprehensive Service Export Register for BIM/CAD engagements containing the signed contract or purchase order, the foreign-currency invoice, the deliverable acceptance record (驗收文件) and the foreign-client master-data file
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / electronic transport document evidencing physical export (required for goods-based export bundles; not applicable to pure offshore service exports)

Inward Remittance Certificate (銀行結匯水單/外匯收入證明), or the equivalent bank SWIFT statement and Wise remittance advice, evidencing receipt of the exact foreign-currency amount from the non-resident counter-party within the permitted collection window

Zero-rated Electronic Uniform Invoice together with the E-Invoice Integration Service Platform transmission record (Turnkey upload acknowledgement) showing the zero-rate indicator and the 7-day transmission compliance stamp

Supporting technical documents — architectural and engineering scope-of-work, design handover schedule, and BIM/IFC project information delivery logs demonstrating that the service was performed in Taiwan but used abroad
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rated export refund claims attract intensified documentary scrutiny, including on-site audit (實地查核) and inquiry into related-party service arrangements. Under Business Tax Act Article 51, fraudulent zero-rating applications, forged export evidence, or over-declared refunds are penalised by up to five times the evaded tax (with a minimum fine of NT$30,000), followed by retrospective clawback of the refunded input VAT plus interest computed from the refund date; serious or repeated violations may lead to suspension or revocation of business and VAT registration. Erroneous zero-rating — for example where the BIM/CAD service is found to benefit a Taiwan-based party or to be re-sourced in Taiwan — is recharacterised as a 5% taxable supply, with reassessment extending three tax years (seven years in fraud cases) plus related interest. Tax Collection Act Article 41 separately criminalises fraudulent tax evasion with imprisonment for up to five years, and suspicious remittance patterns linked to refund claims may additionally trigger Anti-Money-Laundering reporting obligations to the Taiwan FIU.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) as the supreme monetary and financial regulator; delegated foreign exchange administration and enforcement authority vested in the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) and its local branches.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The RMB is convertible on current-account items under a managed floating exchange-rate regime; service trade receipts, profit remittances and documented operational disbursements are permitted through designated foreign-exchange banks once the underlying transaction is verified. Capital-account items remain substantially controlled: foreign-direct-investment capital contributions, cross-border loans, and outbound investments require SAFE registration, a legal capital and use-of-funds inspection, and adherence to the Foreign Investment Negative List. Profit remittance by a WFOE is allowable after completion of statutory annual audit, filing of the audited financial statements, payment of corporate income tax, and fulfilment of withholding obligations, subject to a board resolution declaring distributable profits.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The mandatory foreign-exchange surrender regime was abolished in 2012; there is no statutory fixed conversion ratio for export receipts. However, all export proceeds deriving from current-account transactions, including cross-border CAD/BIM engineering services, must be repatriated to a licensed domestic branch and recorded in the Foreign Exchange Monitoring System. Goods-trade proceeds generally must be credited and settled within 90 days from customs declaration; service-trade fees must be repatriated within the contractual settlement maturity (typically no later than 180 days from invoice issuance unless extended by justification). The WFOE may retain such proceeds in a foreign-currency current account or convert them to RMB at the prevailing market rate; under-declaration, delayed repatriation or non-repatriation triggers SAFE penalties and automatic loss of simplified settlement procedures.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low, with narrow and non-statutory ancillary use only. Offshore digital EMI accounts, such as Wise multi-currency accounts, are not licensed receiving institutions under PRC banking law and cannot function as SAFE-designated receiving banks for inbound capital injection, export-proceeds repatriation, or tax-cleared profit remittance. A WFOE may leverage offshore EMIs for immaterial, non-trade operating expenses only if the underlying transaction is independently documented, the funds are sourced from an already-compliant foreign-exchange account through a licensed domestic bank, and no false representation of the EMI as a clearing rail is made. Using an EMI to bypass the SAFE banking loop creates a structural KYC and anti-money-laundering violation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for the legal representative of a foreign-invested enterprise during corporate account opening at a PRC licensed bank. The legal representative and at least one authorised signatory must appear before the bank's compliance officer in person for biometric capture, original ID verification, and interview. Remote opening via video or through a foreign notary is generally unavailable for a first-time WFOE account. Where the legal representative resides outside mainland China, a Power of Attorney in notarised form and authenticated by the Taiwan notary office and optionally by the China-Entrusted Association could allow an in-country local director to attend, but the majority of state-owned banks will still request a physical appearance of the legal representative for enhanced due diligence on high-risk propositions. The Taiwan shareholder's legalised identification and proof of source of funds are mandatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner resides in Taiwan while operating a PRC WFOE supplying engineering services to Taiwanese/offshore clients; bank flags cross-strait fund flows and potential disguised branch activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Authenticated WFOE business license and Foreign Investment Filing Code; certified constitutional documents and board resolutions appointing the PRC manager; current cross-border service agreements with Taiwanese downstream clients; invoices and receivable ledger; evidence of real and substantive BIM/CAD deliverables (autodesk Revit models, structural drawings, and engineering deliverables logs); payroll and social-insurance records for PRC technical staff; office lease and utility bills; audited financial statements; SAFE Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) registration certificate; latest corporate income tax returns; and the shareholder's legalised personal identification and bank reference letter demonstrating lawful source of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Invoice value is material but the entity has thin track record or minimal tangible assets; bank suspects pass-through invoicing or illegal money movement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete contract life-cycle documentation (request-for-proposal, purchase order, scope-of-work, milestone acceptance certificates); time-and-attendance records and production logs matching deliverables; licensed engineering software licences in the WFOE's name; professional indemnity insurance policy; certificates of completion signed by end-clients; detailed bank statement history projected on accounting-system records; fixed-asset purchase receipts for workstations; and a notarised statutory declaration from the Taiwan counterparty confirming the arm's-length business purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of clear purpose for profit remittance or capital settlements; bank queries whether funds are being returned to the Taiwanese investor as disguised dividend or loan.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution and shareholders' meeting minutes declaring and detailing the remittance purpose; audited balance sheet showing distributable retained earnings; corporate income tax settlement and withholding tax payment vouchers in compliance with the cross-strait tax agreement; a schedule translating retained earnings to declared profits; actual cash-account reconciliation; and an independent auditor's report confirming the profit amount.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The Taiwanese shareholder remits the subscribed registered capital in freely convertible foreign exchange (typically USD or CNY from lawful offshore income) to the WFOE's SAFE-registered foreign-exchange capital account at a designated domestic bank. The remittance instruction must clearly state 'foreign-invested enterprise registered capital contribution', cite the FDI registration code, and satisfy the receiving bank's authenticity check. The receiving bank will verify against the Foreign Investment Information Report and the SAFE Foreign Direct Investment basic information table. After receipt and conversion to RMB, the funds may be used only for the WFOE's permitted scope of operation, including payroll, software licences, sub-contractor fees and office overheads; prohibited repatriation to the Taiwanese investor before regulatory completion and prohibited entry into securities/real-estate investment unless approved.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For settlement of cross-border engineering sub-contracts, software licensing, cloud-computing charges, and qualified royalties, the WFOE executes a corporate wire transfer through its domestic bank over the SWIFT network, normally an MT103 message. Service trade settlements below the USD 50,000 de minimis threshold may follow simplified documentary review; amounts above require submission of the service trade contract, invoice, receipt from the overseas counterparty, tax payment or exemption certificate, and the Cross-Border RMB/SEZ form. Where a supplier requires a documentary guarantee, a Commercial Letter of Credit advised by the Taiwanese beneficiary's bank can be issued, but for service transactions an L/C is rarely used because deliverables are intangible. Profit distribution to the Taiwanese shareholder follows the same SWIFT rail, with the bank requiring confirmation that enterprise income tax and any withholding tax have been cleared.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable foreign exchange forwards (USD/RMB, EUR/RMB, HKD/RMB) with real trade document support through a licensed PRC bank
Cross-currency swaps and interest-rate swaps for long-term capital and loan rebalancing, registered under SAFE and approved under the local lead-bank framework
Plain-vanilla FX options (call and put) transacted onshore against real current-account exposure, including carbon-neutral engineering service fee hedging
Participating forwards and average-rate forwards offered by onshore banks as structured variants of deliverable forwards

Offshore RMB non-deliverable forwards (NDFs), permissible only where the PRC bank observes exceptional pilot status and the entity has obtained a formal SAFE no-objection letter; standard onshore access is otherwise disallowed, and the WFOE must rely on deliverable instruments against USD/HKD rather than NDFs

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business Report and Financial Statements (Shareholder Approval and Filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) – Company Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year end + 6 months (June 30) for shareholder approval; file with MOEA within 15 days after approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: NT$10,000–50,000 fine for late filing; repeated noncompliance may trigger administrative dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Finance – National Taxation Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Surcharge of 1% per month on unpaid tax (max 5%); underreported tax penalty of 2× of shortfall; nonfiling penalty up to NT$54,000 plus tax lien and eventual strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By June 30 annually around fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Noncompliance restricts foreign exchange remittance and future investment approvals; administrative fine of up to NT$120,000 under Foreign Investment Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: February 25 for prior-year annual summary (in addition to monthly/bi-monthly filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty equal to 15% of unpaid tax plus daily interest; administrative revocation for persistent nonfiling

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Companies with paid-in capital exceeding NT$30 million (approx. USD 1 million) require certified public accountant audit; also mandatory for financial institutions and companies listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange or TPEx
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan IFRS (TIFRS) for public companies; Business Entity Accounting Act GAAP (FAS) for private enterprises

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate annual UBO public filing in Taiwan; shareholder ownership details must be disclosed in the annual Foreign Investment Report to MOEAIC, and any shareholding transfers must be updated in the Register of Members promptly

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general corporate income tax holidays for WFOEs in Taiwan; standard rate is 25% on profit-seeking enterprise income (營利事業所得稅). Qualified R&D expenditures may be eligible for an investment tax credit of 15% up to 30% of the current-year tax payable, subject to limits. Domestic profit distribution to a non-resident corporate shareholder is subject to withholding tax at 21% (or 10% for non-resident individuals), unless reduced under an applicable DTA or the Cross-Strait Agreement.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return (營利事業所得稅結算申報書) Form 15, filed electronically via the Ministry of Finance e-Filing System (電子申報繳稅服務網) with supporting financial statements; quarterly advance payments (預估暫繳) are required.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing due by the 5th month after the fiscal year-end (generally May 31 for calendar-year filers). Provisional payments due by September 30 (for the preceding six months) and December 31 (second half).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all Taiwan-source revenue for services rendered or used in Taiwan; for China-related projects, assess whether income is Taiwan-source or China-source under the Cross-Strait Agreement.

Net figure carried to gross income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after loss carryforward and exemptions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the five-year loss carryforward (for losses incurred before 2021; post-2021 losses carry forward 10 years) to the extent of Taiwan-source income.
Compute 25% of taxable income; check if any preferential rate applies (e.g., qualifying innovative enterprises may benefit from reduced rate on certain income).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Less: Investment tax credits and foreign tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credit any Taiwan-sourced withholding tax and, if applicable, foreign tax paid on foreign-source income included in the return, subject to the maximum foreign tax credit limit.
Net tax due after advance payments; remit with the return.

WFOEs with related-party transactions meeting the threshold (typically NT$100 million in aggregate between related parties or NT$50 million with a Taiwan-related party) must file a transfer pricing report with the annual CIT return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without extension: additional 10% of the unpaid tax if filed after the deadline but before delinquency; 20% if filed after an investigation. After delinquency notice: additional 3% surcharge for every 30 days, up to 10%; then forced collection. Interest accrues daily at the postal 2-year time-deposit rate plus 1%. Failure to file without just cause can result in an additional tax of 10% to 20% and up to NT$30,000 in per-item fines.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Taiwan does not have a full double tax agreement with China but has the Cross-Strait Agreement for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (生效於2010年, limited administrative arrangement). To invoke reduced withholding, the Taiwanese-resident parent must obtain a Certificate of Residence (COR) from the Taiwan tax authority and submit an application for the reduced withholding rate to the PRC tax authority (for dividends from the China WFOE). For dividends paid from China to Taiwan, the PRC withholding tax rate is 10% under domestic law, but the Cross-Strait Agreement provides a 5% rate if the Taiwan parent is the beneficial owner of at least 25% of the WFOE's shares for 12 consecutive months prior to the dividend payment. The Taiwan parent must apply for the reduced rate via the PRC taxpayer's withholding agent using Form 1040-1 (Non-resident Taxpayer) and provide the COR, a beneficial ownership declaration, and certificate of residence. For profit repatriation from Taiwan to Taiwan-parent, the dividend withholding tax is 21% on the remittance to a foreign enterprise, unless a treaty (rarely applicable) reduces the rate. The administrative protocol requires submission of the DTA relief application to the Taiwan tax authority before/at the time of filing the non-resident dividend withholding return (繳款書). In practice, the tax authority may require a ruling or advance approval for cross-strait treaty relief due to political and legal complexities; therefore, many Taiwanese investors simply pay the 10% PRC withholding on dividends from the WFOE and the 21% Taiwan withholding on Taiwan-sourced profits. The recipient must provide a valid TRC (Taiwan residence certificate) and a notarized beneficial ownership statement; the PRC side requires the tax authority's acceptance and issuance of a 'Tax Resident Certificate' of Taiwan. Failure to file the DTA relief application before the distribution results in the full 21% statutory rate being withheld and subject to later refund via a claim process.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: For payments from a Taiwan WFOE to a foreign (including mainland China) licensor: royalty withholding tax is 20% (increased from 15% after 2018 in some cases), but a 10% may apply under certain treaties; interest withholding is 20% for non-residents without a branch; under the Cross-Strait Agreement, interest from China to Taiwan is generally limited to 7% of the gross amount (or 10% for interest from financial institutions), and royalties are limited to 10% of gross royalties (or 7% for equipment use). In Taiwan, payments to a mainland Chinese enterprise for royalties are also subject to 10% withholding tax under the Cross-Strait Agreement (if the recipient provides a certificate of residence), otherwise 20% applies. For debt interest paid by a Taiwan WFOE to a mainland China parent, the general rate is 20% unless the China creditor is a qualified financial institution and the beneficial owner, in which case the rate may be reduced to 7% under the Cross-Strait Agreement; similarly, for Taiwan interest paid to a non-resident, the statutory rate is 20% unless a treaty reduces it.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: For Taiwan: related-party transactions exceeding NT$100 million in aggregate or NT$50 million with a single related party trigger mandatory transfer pricing documentation (Master File and Local File). For the China WFOE (paying/charging fees to Taiwan): no explicit statutory threshold, but the PRC's implementation rules require contemporaneous documentation (Local File and Master File) when related-party transactions exceed RMB 100 million (approx. NT$440 million) in a year, and a relevant file is required when the annual amount exceeds RMB 40 million for a single controlled transaction. tax authorities may require a TP report even under the threshold in high-risk cases.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan has adopted the profit-seeking enterprise economic substance principles via the 'Practical Guidelines for the Examination of Profit-Seeking Enterprise’s Negative Income' and the general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR) under Article 66-8 of the Income Tax Act, allowing the tax authority to re-characterize transactions lacking economic substance. In China, the PRC GAAR and the 'reasonable allocation of profit' rules under Special Tax Adjustments require a WFOE to demonstrate that it performs meaningful functions, employs personnel, bears risks, and controls assets, especially when making service or royalty payments to a related Taiwan party. Both jurisdictions require the substantive operations doctrine: a mere conduit or contract manufacturer without real functions may be disregarded or re-characterized.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underreporting or omitting Taiwan-source CAD/BIM revenue; fabricating expenses; using shell invoices to inflate costs; misclassifying income as capital gains to avoid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Taiwan Income Tax Act, an additional tax of up to 2x (but not less than 15%) of the evaded tax amount is imposed, plus fines up to NT$60,000; criminal sanctions may include imprisonment up to 5 years and a fine up to NT$6 million under the Tax Evasion Punishment Act; in practice, authorities can impose an additional tax of up to 5x of the understated tax for serious violations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A legal representative or finance officer who willfully files a false return may be subject to criminal prosecution; directors who sign the return are liable for the accuracy of the filing; tax evasion can lead to travel bans (境管) and seizure of personal assets if the corporate tax liability cannot be collected from the company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Manipulating intercompany pricing for CAD/BIM services between the Taiwan parent and the China WFOE to shift profits out of Taiwan; paying excessive royalties or management fees to a China-related party without documenting arm's length.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Taiwan tax authority may make a transfer pricing adjustment and impose an additional tax of 10%–20% of the adjusted income; penalty of 200% of the additional tax if the taxpayer failed to file a TP report or keep documentation; in China, the adjustment can result in a 10% to 50% penalty on the underpaid tax and a 5-year lookback extended to 10 years for special tax adjustments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable for the company's tax debts if they are found to have committed fraud or gross negligence in approving artificial transfer prices; in both China and Taiwan, directors can face criminal penalties if they knowingly cause tax evasion; civil liability may extend to restoring any unjust enrichment from the tax authority.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Taiwan WFOE without substantive staff, office, or operational control; using it solely to receive invoices and route payments, or claiming tax benefits while failing to demonstrate business purpose and actual commercial functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under GAAR, the tax authority may disregard the corporate personality or re-allocate income to the true substance; the company may be derecognized for tax purposes, triggering full assessment of income at 25%, plus penalties; the beneficial owner status for treaty relief is denied, and dividend WHT is recaptured and penalized.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be subject to partnership-style liability if the company is deemed a sham; a court may pierce the corporate veil to hold shareholders/directors personally liable for unpaid taxes; in China, legal representatives are automatically put on a 'blacklist' (失信被執行人) and banned from leaving China, and in severe cases face imprisonment for fraudulent tax enforcement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering (AML) / Illegal Foreign Exchange Settlement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving payments from China or Taiwan through unauthorized personal bank accounts, splitting transactions to avoid reporting thresholds, using underground banks to move funds, or accepting cash without documenting the source; invoicing services with false descriptions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Taiwan's Money Laundering Control Act, fines range from NT$500,000 to NT$100 million and imprisonment of up to 2 years for individuals; in China, under the Anti-Money Laundering Law, fines up to RMB 5 million and criminal liability under PRC Criminal Law Art. 191 for money laundering (5 to 10 years imprisonment); the State Administration of Foreign Exchange may impose a fine of 30% of the illegal foreign exchange amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or knowingly benefit from illegal remittance channels are personally liable; they can be criminally prosecuted for money laundering, face imprisonment, criminal fines, and personal asset forfeiture; when the corporate entity is a shell, courts may pierce the veil to reach personal assets of the controlling shareholder.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File Transfer Pricing Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Not preparing and filing the Taiwan Transfer Pricing Report (Form 20) or the China contemporaneous TP documentation when the statutory thresholds are exceeded; failing to update the Master File/Local File annually.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: In Taiwan, failure to file the TP report can trigger an additional tax of 2x the understated tax and a fine of NT$10,000 to NT$50,000; the tax authority may disallow the loss carryforward and adjust the deemed arm's length profit. In China, the penalty is up to RMB 100,000 for non-compliance, and the tax authority may apply a 5% or 10% penalty on the underpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the WFOE may be deemed to have knowingly or negligently failed to fulfill a statutory compliance obligation, leading to personal joint liability for the subsequent tax adjustment if the company is insolvent; in extreme cases, the legal representative may be criminally prosecuted for refusal to pay taxes after a final administrative order.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Late Filing / Non-Payment of Corporate Income Tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Missing the May 31 annual CIT deadline or underpaying the provisional tax installments by more than 10% without adequate cause.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Additional tax of 10%–20% of the unpaid amount, plus daily interest at the 1-year postal deposit rate plus 1%, compounded monthly; if the return is not filed and the tax remains unpaid, the collection agency may escalate to enforcement proceedings and potentially apply a 3% surcharge for every 30 days of delinquency, capped at 10%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative (負責人) of a WFOE is required to pay the tax from the company's assets; if the company fails to do so, the tax authority may apply to restrict the legal representative from leaving Taiwan or China; willful non-compliance may result in compulsory detention or criminal sanctions for the representative (e.g., imprisonment up to 2 years) if deemed a refusal to pay.
